briefing: SAMPLE BRIEFING (mock mode). 1) Web search as an agent tool: Claude's API offers a server-side web search tool with a max_uses limit, so agents can look things up and cite sources. Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool 2) The Model Context Protocol (MCP) keeps growing as the common way to plug tools and data into AI apps. Source: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/ 3) Python's json module remains the standard way to parse structured model output. Source: https://docs.python.org/3/library/json.html

plan.summary: [Sample] Web search for agents, an MCP refresher, a new lesson on agents that cite sources, and two new glossary terms.

news.title: [Sample] AI agents can search the web and cite sources
news.summary: Developers can give Claude a built-in web search tool. The model decides when to search, reads the results and cites where its facts came from. A max_uses setting caps how many searches it can make.
news.why: Citing sources is how you spot hallucinations - always click through on facts that matter.

news.title: [Sample] MCP: the 'USB port' for AI tools
news.summary: The Model Context Protocol is an open standard for connecting AI apps to tools and data. Many AI apps and coding assistants can now plug into the same MCP servers.
news.why: Learning tool use once means you can connect AI to almost anything.

news.summary: This item should be rejected because its source never appeared in the search results.

glossary.def: A tool that runs on the AI provider's side, like web search, so your code doesn't have to run it.
A link to the source an AI used for a fact, so you can check it yourself.

block_updates.x: **MCP (Model Context Protocol)** is an open standard for packaging tools and data sources so many AI apps can plug into them - like a USB port for AI tools. Once you understand tool use, MCP is the same idea at scale, and a growing number of AI apps and coding assistants support it.

new_lessons.title: Agents that cite their sources
new_lessons.summary: Give an agent a search tool, keep track of where each fact came from, and show citations.

blocks.x: Trustworthy agents **show their sources**. When an agent looks something up, your code can record *where* each fact came from and show it with the answer - so people can check it.

items: Search or look up a fact with a tool
Keep the source next to the result
Show the answer with numbered citations
If there is no source, say so

blocks.x: Real APIs can return citations for you. Your job is to *display* them and to treat "no source" as a reason to be careful.

takeaways: Record a source for every fact an agent finds.
No source? Say so instead of guessing.

quiz.q: Why should an agent show its sources?
options: So people can check the facts

quiz.q: What should an agent do when it finds no source?
Where is the best place to keep a fact's source?
options: Right next to the result in your data
quiz.why: Keeping them together makes showing citations easy.
